audit_findings.title: Cash add-back assumes foreign and operating cash is fully distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $212.101m bridge exposure ($8.67/share and 35.6% of $595m base equity value); $128.0m of cash was held by foreign subsidiaries ($5.23/share and 60.3% of the add-back); required haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the cash and short-term-investment bridge added to operating value; any recurring operating-cash requirement could also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At January 31, 2026, the Company had no deferred tax liability for substantially all of the undistributed foreign earnings of approximately $ 253.4 m illion because the Company intends to permanently reinvest such earnings in its foreign operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $212.101m add-back is demonstrated, but the filing does not demonstrate that all of it is excess or distributable. The $262.9m of permanently reinvested foreign earnings is not itself a cash balance or proof of trapping, although the filed $128.0m foreign cash balance makes jurisdictional availability a material unresolved issue. Even a partial haircut could materially change per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 31, 2026 cash and short-term-investment schedule by entity and jurisdiction, quantify minimum operating cash, restrictions and repatriation leakage, and rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Licensed-brand concentration makes renewals a central forecast dependency
audit_findings.magnitude: Licensed brands were 58.3% of FY2026 net sales, or approximately $391.4m of $671.3m; the sales attributable specifically to Hugo Boss and Calvin Klein are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: License loss or worse renewal terms would reduce revenue, margins, OE growth and the earnings supporting terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, the Company's licensed brands represented 58.3% of the Company’s net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration and stated December 31, 2026 expirations are demonstrated, while nonrenewal or adverse economics remain possibilities rather than established losses. Because the DCF assigns 46.3%-51.5% of operating value to terminal value and assumes continuing earnings, unresolved licenses covering part of a business whose licensed brands generate most sales are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain executed Hugo Boss and Calvin Klein extensions and their royalty, minimum-sales, advertising and termination terms; quantify each brand's sales and OE contribution and rerun all scenarios for nonrenewal and adverse renewal economics.

audit_findings.title: Large minimum license commitments may not flex with the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $269.6m of gross minimum commitments over six years; incremental cost beyond expenses already embedded in OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-flexing minimum royalties, advertising, endorsement or service payments would compress forecast OE, especially when sales decline.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the total amount of the Company’s minimum commitments related to its license agreements and endorsement agreements, which includes service agreements, was $ 269.6 million, payable in the next six years .
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are contractual and large relative to the $382m base operating value, but they cannot be deducted wholesale because current related expenses are already reflected in historical OE. The record lacks the annual schedule and contractual thresholds needed to determine whether forecast expenses fall below the minimums, so the effect may be material but cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Map each annual minimum by agreement and cost category to the expenses embedded in OE, then rerun each scenario using the greater of modeled variable expense or the applicable contractual minimum, including termination rights.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE may be based on superseded financial statements
audit_findings.magnitude: The affected supplied OE observations are $92.4m for 2022, $93.3m for 2023 and $44.5m for 2024; correction to those amounts is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Corrected revenue, allowances, taxes, working capital and NCI could change historical OE, RONTA and the evidence used to select growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of this material weakness, the Company restated previously issued financial statements for fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, as well as the interim periods within fiscal year 2025 and fiscal year 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The restatement is demonstrated, but use of superseded figures in the supplied OE series is not. The $27.2m valuation anchor is the latest actual rather than a historical trend, so this issue does not automatically alter the anchor; nevertheless, corrected history could change the volatility assessment, RONTA and growth judgments. Direction and materiality cannot be established without tracing the inputs.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate FY2022-FY2024 OE from the restated statements, reconcile each result to the supplied series, recompute RONTA and the historical-growth evidence, and rerun scenarios only if those inputs or judgments change.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may retain material nonrecurring charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.1m pre-tax, equal to 18.8% of the $27.2m anchor; if fully nonrecurring, approximately $4.0m after tax using the filed 21.8% rate, implying about $42.4m-$66.1m or $1.73-$2.70/share of scenario-value sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing genuinely nonrecurring charges would increase anchor OE and proportionally increase projected OE, operating PV and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The operating income in the Watch and Accessory Brands segment for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, included a pre-tax charge of $ 1.5 million related to the Company's cost-savings initiative and a pre-tax charge of $ 3.6 million of costs related to the investigation of allegations of misconduct within the Dubai branch of the Company's Swiss subsidiary.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1.5m cost-savings charge and $3.6m investigation charge are demonstrated, but their treatment in the OE calculation and the recurring portion of related compliance costs are unresolved. Their scale relative to the anchor makes classification material. The sensitivity is conditional, not evidence that the entire $5.1m should be removed.
audit_findings.action: Trace both charges through the $27.2m OE calculation, identify completed versus continuing costs, normalize only the demonstrated nonrecurring after-tax portion, and rerun bear, base and bull values plus buy-below prices.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash may include amounts attributable to noncontrolling owners
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed noncontrolling interest was $1.601m, equal to about $0.07/share and 0.27% of $595m base equity value; cash attributable to noncontrolling owners is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any non-parent share of consolidated cash should be removed from the bridge or offset by an explicit NCI deduction so the numerator matches parent-attributable OE and shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Noncontrolling interest is recognized as equity in the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets and represents ownership interests in the Company’s subsidiaries held by third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of noncontrolling ownership is demonstrated, but the record does not identify how much of the $212.101m bridge cash sits in partly owned subsidiaries or whether the $0.3m stakes adjustment addresses it. The recognized NCI balance is small compared with base equity value, but it is not necessarily a ceiling on the gross cash attributable to minority owners, so materiality cannot be conclusively dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Identify cash and short-term investments held by each partly owned subsidiary, apply the outside ownership percentage, reconcile the result to the $1.601m NCI balance and $0.3m stakes adjustment, and rerun the bridge for any uncovered amount.
